Jules (customer): Hey team — we've got a customer on our Dedicated instance seeing repeated logouts after enabling device trust. They re-auth, but subsequent API calls to embeddings endpoint get 401 invalid_token. Happens across browsers and curl.

Alex (Support): Sorry you're running into this. Can you confirm whether the 401 happens immediately after MFA re-enroll, or only after some time? Any errors in the browser console or server logs?

Jules (customer): Immediately after re-enroll. Steps I took: 1) go to Settings -> Security, 2) toggle device trust on, 3) complete MFA, 4) call /v1/embeddings with Bearer <access_token> -> 401 JSON: {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"token revoked or expired"}. Re-issuing a new access token from the web UI fixes it for ~30s then back to 401.

Alex (Support): Thanks. Can you paste the exact curl you used (feel free to redact token), and whether this is our hosted API or Dedicated/private?

Jules (customer): Dedicated deployment in eu-west. Curl:

```
curl -X POST "https://internal-eu.customer.redwood/api/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-abc","input":"hello"}'
```

No browser console errors. Server logs show a few lines around the 401: `auth: token validation failed for token=*** reason=revoked device_update=true` then `session: cookie TTL remaining=0`.

Mira (SRE): Reproduced locally against staging Dedicated with device-trust toggle. Observed session cookie being rotated but old refresh tokens are being marked revoked on device metadata change. However our rotation path was supposed to gracefully rebind cookies and refresh tokens; looks like the cookie domain attribute dropped `SameSite=None` in the reissue, causing browser to drop cookie on cross-subdomain calls from the control-plane proxy.

Sam (Auth Eng): Hmm — two things to confirm: 1) are we invalidating all refresh tokens on device-trust changes (by design yes), 2) are we issuing a new refresh token and setting the session cookie in the same response where MFA completes? If the client does an immediate API call using an access token issued before the new cookie is set, our token introspection can return revoked.

Alex (Support): Customer says new access token works for ~30s then fails. That suggests there might be an async background job revoking tokens or a TTL mismatch.

Mira (SRE): Confirmed: there is a background job (device-trust-audit) that reconciles device metadata and sets refresh_token.revoked=true if mismatched. The job runs on a short interval in Dedicated (30s). When device trust is toggled, the UI issues new tokens and sets cookie, but the job runs and marks older tokens revoked — and because our cookie reissue path has SameSite missing for a subset of requests, some proxied calls don't include the new cookie; token introspection then sees an access token that references a revoked refresh token and returns invalid_token.

Sam (Auth Eng): That explains the ~30s window. Two mitigations: 1) short-term: pause the audit job on the customer's cluster until we patch SameSite handling; 2) longer-term: ensure device-trust flows rotate tokens atomically and change the audit job to not revoke tokens until the new session is observed from the same client.

Jules (customer): Pausing job sounds fine for us short-term. We'll take instructions. Also, can you confirm if this affects API keys or only OAuth sessions? We're using OAuth SSO.

Alex (Support): This only impacts OAuth access/refresh flows and session cookies — API keys are unaffected.

Mira (SRE): I can pause device-trust-audit on the customer's Dedicated cluster ASAP. Doing it now.

session-bot: device-trust-audit job on cluster customer-dedicated-eu paused by Mira at 2026-03-15T14:12:40Z

Mira (SRE): Paused. Jules — can you re-enroll device-trust steps and confirm behavior now?

Jules (customer): Re-enrolled. So far stable, made several calls to embeddings + chat, no 401. Thanks.

Sam (Auth Eng): I'll prepare a patch to ensure the cookie is re-set with `SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly; Domain=.customer.redwood` during the MFA/device-trust response path, and add an atomic token swap so the old refresh token is only revoked after the new session is confirmed. Also will instrument a metric for mismatched cookie attributes.

Alex (Support): ETA on patch?

Sam (Auth Eng): Small change — PR up today, staging deploy tonight, can push to Dedicated tomorrow morning. Adding a feature flag to toggle behavior per-customer if we need a hotfix.

deploy-bot: PR #5281 (auth: set SameSite=None on session reissue + atomic rotation) merged to main by Sam at 2026-03-15T18:40:12Z

deploy-bot: Rolling deploy to staging initiated.

Mira (SRE): Verified staging: no regression, cookie attributes correct, and device-trust flow doesn't produce a short-lived 401. I'm scheduling a canary to the affected customer's cluster with the feature-flag off by default, then enable for them after smoke tests.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy to customer-dedicated-eu scheduled for 2026-03-16T02:00:00Z

Alex (Support): Jules — we'll keep you posted and coordinate a maintenance window for the canary flip. In the meantime, leaving the audit job paused should be a safe mitigation. Thanks for raising this and for the quick repro steps. :thumbsup:

Jules (customer): Appreciate it. Please let me know if you want logs or to keep the ticket open until the canary is enabled.

Alex (Support): We'll leave it open and update the ticket once canary is live.

Mira (SRE): Follow-up actions added to internal tracking: (1) hotfix verify for cookie domain and SameSite, (2) make audit job resilient to in-flight rotations, (3) add per-customer feature-flag for rotation semantics.

Sam (Auth Eng): Will also add an integration test that simulates device trust toggle + immediate API calls to prevent regression.

session-bot: ticket#CUST-20432 updated: mitigation applied, pending canary.

Jules (customer): Thanks everyone — confirmed stable after the pause. Will wait for your canary notification.

Alex (Support): Closing loop for now, will re-open thread when canary flips.
